18.1: Arjuna's last question: tell me the truth about renunciation and about relinquishment, and the difference between them.
18.2: Renunciation is giving up actions prompted by desire; relinquishment is abandoning the fruit of all actions.
18.3: Some thinkers say action should be given up as evil; others say acts of sacrifice, charity and austerity should not be abandoned.
18.4: Hear My conclusion on relinquishment: it is declared to be of three kinds.
18.5: Acts of sacrifice, charity and austerity should not be given up but performed — they purify the wise.
18.6: Even these should be done with attachment and the fruit abandoned — that is My certain and highest view.
18.7: Renunciation of a prescribed duty is not proper; giving it up through delusion is declared tamasic.
18.8: One who gives up action as painful, from fear of bodily trouble, performs rajasic relinquishment and gains nothing by it.
18.9: But when a prescribed duty is done simply because it ought to be done, abandoning attachment and fruit, that relinquishment is sattvic.
18.10: The wise relinquisher, filled with sattva, doubts cut, neither hates disagreeable work nor is attached to agreeable work.
18.11: No embodied being can give up action entirely; the one who gives up the fruit is the true relinquisher.
18.12: The threefold fruit of action — desirable, undesirable and mixed — accrues after death to non-relinquishers, but never to renunciates.
18.13: Learn from Me the five causes of the accomplishment of all action, as declared in Sankhya.
18.14: The seat, the doer, the various organs, the different functions, and divine providence — these are the five.
18.15: Whatever action a person performs with body, speech or mind, right or wrong, these five are its causes.
18.16: One who, through an untrained understanding, sees the pure Self as the sole doer does not see rightly.
18.17: One free of the sense of ego, whose intelligence is not tainted, though he kills these people, does not kill and is not bound.
18.18: Knowledge, the object of knowledge and the knower are the threefold impulse to action; the organ, the action and the doer are its threefold basis.
18.19: Knowledge, action and doer are of three kinds according to the gunas; hear them duly described.
18.20: Sattvic knowledge sees one imperishable being in all beings, undivided in the divided.
18.21: Rajasic knowledge sees, by reason of separateness, different beings of various kinds in all beings.
18.22: Tamasic knowledge clings to one effect as if it were everything, without reason, without truth and trivial.
18.23: Sattvic action is ordained, free of attachment, done without love or hatred by one who desires no fruit.
18.24: Rajasic action is done with great effort by one seeking desires or prompted by egoism.
18.25: Tamasic action is undertaken through delusion, without regard to consequence, loss, injury or one's own capacity.
18.26: The sattvic doer is free from attachment and egoism, endowed with firmness and zeal, unaffected by success or failure.
18.27: The rajasic doer is passionate, greedy for the fruit, cruel, impure, moved by joy and sorrow.
18.28: The tamasic doer is undisciplined, vulgar, obstinate, deceitful, malicious, lazy, despondent and procrastinating.
18.29: Now hear the threefold division of intellect and firmness according to the gunas, described fully and distinctly.
18.30: Sattvic intellect knows the paths of action and renunciation, what should and should not be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and liberation.
18.31: Rajasic intellect distinguishes wrongly between dharma and adharma, and between what should and should not be done.
18.32: Tamasic intellect, enveloped in darkness, takes adharma to be dharma and sees all things perversely.
18.33: Sattvic firmness holds mind, life-breath and senses steady through unswerving yoga.
18.34: Rajasic firmness holds to duty, pleasure and wealth with attachment and desire for their fruit.
18.35: Tamasic firmness is that by which a dull person does not give up sleep, fear, grief, despair and conceit.
18.36: Now hear of the three kinds of happiness, in which one delights through practice and comes to the end of pain.
18.37: Sattvic happiness is like poison at first and nectar at the end, born of the serenity of one's own mind.
18.38: Rajasic happiness arises from the contact of the senses with objects — nectar at first and poison at the end.
18.39: Tamasic happiness deludes the self from beginning to end, arising from sleep, indolence and heedlessness.
18.40: There is no being on earth or among the gods free from these three qualities born of nature.
18.41: The duties of the four orders are distributed according to the qualities born of their own natures.
18.42: The brahmin's duties: serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forbearance, uprightness, knowledge, realisation and belief in the beyond.
18.43: The warrior's duties: heroism, vigour, firmness, resourcefulness, not fleeing from battle, generosity and leadership.
18.44: The merchant's duties are agriculture, cattle-rearing and trade; the servant's duty is service — all born of their own nature.
18.45: Devoted to one's own duty, a person attains perfection; hear how such devotion brings it about.
18.46: By worshipping through one's own duty the One from whom all beings arise and by whom all this is pervaded, one attains perfection.
18.47: Better one's own duty though imperfect than another's well performed; doing the duty ordained by one's own nature, one incurs no sin.
18.48: One should not abandon the duty of one's birth even if flawed; all undertakings are clouded by defect as fire is by smoke.
18.49: One whose intellect is unattached everywhere, self-conquered, free of longing, attains by renunciation the supreme state beyond action.
18.50: Learn briefly how one who has attained perfection reaches Brahman, the supreme consummation of knowledge.
18.51: Endowed with a pure intellect, controlling the self with firmness, relinquishing sound and other objects, casting aside attraction and hatred —
18.52: — dwelling in solitude, eating little, speech, body and mind controlled, ever engaged in meditation and dispassion —
18.53: — having abandoned egoism, power, arrogance, desire, anger and possessions, free from 'mine' and at peace — one is fit to become Brahman.
18.54: Having become Brahman, serene, one neither grieves nor desires; the same to all beings, one attains supreme devotion to Me.
18.55: By devotion one knows Me in truth, what and who I am; then, having known Me in essence, one enters into Me.
18.56: Ever performing all actions and taking refuge in Me, one attains by My grace the eternal, imperishable abode.
18.57: Mentally surrendering all actions to Me, holding Me as the highest, resorting to the yoga of understanding, fix your mind on Me always.
18.58: Fixing your mind on Me, you will overcome all obstacles by My grace; but if from egoism you will not listen, you will perish.
18.59: If, filled with egoism, you think 'I will not fight', your resolve is vain — nature will compel you.
18.60: Bound by your own nature and by your own karma, what you do not wish to do through delusion, you will do helplessly.
18.61: The Lord dwells in the hearts of all beings, causing them to revolve as if mounted on a machine, by His power.
18.62: Take refuge in Him with all your being; by His grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.
18.63: Thus the knowledge more secret than all secrets has been declared; reflect on it fully and then do as you choose.
18.64: Hear again My supreme word, the most secret of all: you are greatly beloved of Me, therefore I will tell you what is good for you.
18.65: Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, sacrifice to Me, bow to Me; you will come to Me — I promise you truly, for you are dear to Me.
18.66: The final surrender: abandon all duties and take refuge in Me alone; I will free you from all sins — do not grieve.
18.67: This is never to be spoken to one without austerity or devotion, who does not wish to hear, or who speaks ill of Me.
18.68: One who teaches this supreme secret to My devotees, with supreme devotion to Me, shall doubtless come to Me.
18.69: There is none among people who does dearer service to Me, nor shall any be dearer to Me on earth.
18.70: One who studies this sacred dialogue of ours worships Me with the sacrifice of knowledge — that is My view.
18.71: Even one who listens with faith and without scoffing is freed and attains the happy worlds of the righteous.
18.72: Krishna's check: have you heard this with a concentrated mind? Has your delusion born of ignorance been destroyed?
18.73: Arjuna's answer, the whole teaching in one line: my delusion is gone, I have regained memory, I stand firm, doubt-free — I will do your word.
18.74: Sanjaya: thus I heard this wondrous dialogue between Krishna and the great-souled Arjuna, causing my hair to stand on end.
18.75: By the grace of Vyasa I heard this supreme and secret yoga directly from the Lord of yoga Himself.
18.76: Remembering again and again this wonderful and holy dialogue, I rejoice again and again.
18.77: And remembering again and again that most wondrous form of Hari, great is my wonder and I rejoice again and again.
18.78: The closing verse: wherever there is Krishna the Lord of yoga and Arjuna the archer, there are prosperity, victory, welfare and firm policy.
